step: Go to Settings, tap Connections, and then tap Wi-Fi.
note: Not DL-0513: that is Intelligent Wi-Fi, a different page.

step: Turn on Wi-Fi so the phone can reach the email server.
note: Not DL-0310: that toggles Wi-Fi scanning, not Wi-Fi itself.

step: Go to Settings, tap Display, and then tap the switch next to Touch sensitivity.
note: Matches data/fixtures/touch_lag.

step: Navigate to Settings, tap Display, and then tap the switch next to Touch sensitivity to disable it.
note: Matches data/fixtures/touch_lag.

step: Go to Settings, tap Display, and then tap Navigation bar.
note: Matches data/fixtures/touch_multi_intent.

step: Select Buttons to turn off full screen gestures.
note: No entry for the Buttons option itself; the navigation bar page is the correct destination.

step: From Settings, search for and select Screen timeout.
note: DL-0471 is a monitoring entry with no navigable screen, so it is not acceptable here.

step: Navigate to Settings, search for and select Factory data reset, and then tap Factory data reset again.
note: Catalog gap. DL-0022 is the AUTO factory reset, not Factory data reset, so returning it is wrong.

step: Tap Settings, and then tap Phone aspect ratio.
note: Catalog gap: no aspect ratio entry exists.

step: Swipe down from the top of the screen and tap Smart View to mirror the display.
note: Catalog gap and a Quick settings tile rather than a Settings screen.

step: Navigate to Settings, tap Apps, select your email app, tap Storage, and then tap Clear cache.
note: Catalog gap: per-app storage screens are not in the catalog. data/fixtures/email_not_responding uses the dummy link for this same step.

step: Restart the phone into Safe mode to check for app conflicts.
note: A hardware button sequence, so no deeplink is appropriate. Category is critical.

step: Open Settings, tap Advanced features, and review the feature list.
note: Catalog gap: the Advanced features menu itself has no entry.

step: Tap Multi window, and then turn on Multi window for all apps.
note: DL-0247 (multi window menu) is a defensible second choice, so it is acceptable.

step: Swipe left to open the Edge panel and turn Edge panels on.
Open Settings, tap Display, and raise the brightness slider.
note: Not DL-0470: that is a monitoring entry, not a screen.

step: Turn on adaptive brightness so the screen adjusts to the light around you.
Open Settings, tap Battery, and then turn on Power saving.
Open Settings, tap Battery, and then turn off Power saving.
Open Settings, tap Battery, tap Charging, and turn on Battery protection.
Open Settings, tap Battery, tap Charging, and then turn on Fast charging.
note: Not DL-0406: that is fast WIRELESS charging. BM25 ranks the wireless entry first.

step: Open Settings, tap Battery, tap Charging, and then turn off Fast wireless charging.
Open Settings, tap Lock screen, and then turn off Always On Display.
screen: Settings > Lock screen > Always On Display
note: Not DL-0407: that is charging information ON the Always On Display, a sub-option.

step: Open Settings, tap Battery, tap Background usage limits, and then turn off Adaptive battery.
note: Message reads 'Adaptive Display' but the description is adaptive battery: match on description.

step: Open Settings, tap Notifications, tap Advanced settings, and then turn on Show battery percentage.
note: DL-0518 and DL-0552 are duplicate entries for the same screen; either is correct.

step: Open Settings, tap Connections, and turn off Bluetooth if no accessory is paired.
note: Not DL-0042 (Bluetooth scanning) and not DL-0100 (tethering), both of which outrank it on BM25.

step: Open Settings, tap Software update, and then tap Download and install.
note: Catalog gap. DL-0024 is auto update of system configurations, a different screen. Category is critical.

step: Open Settings, tap Battery and device care, and then tap Storage.
screen: Settings > Battery and device care > Storage
note: Catalog gap: no Storage screen entry, only Storage Share and the Device care shortcut toggle.

step: Open Settings, tap Display, and turn on Dark mode to reduce glare.
note: Catalog gap: only the Dark mode schedule and dim wallpaper sub-screens exist.

step: Open Settings, tap Display, and turn on Auto rotate so the screen follows the device.
note: Catalog gap: only 'rotate to landscape mode' exists, which is a different setting.

step: Open Settings, tap Display, and turn on Eye comfort shield to cut blue light.
Open Settings, tap Display, and tap Screen mode to change the colour profile.
Open Settings, tap Display, and increase the font size so text is readable.
note: Catalog gap: only the Bold font sub-screen exists under font size.

step: Open Settings, tap Security and privacy, and confirm that Camera access is allowed.
screen: Settings > Security and privacy > Camera access

step: Swipe down from the top of the screen and tap the Flashlight tile to test the flash.
note: A Quick settings tile with no Settings screen behind it.

step: Open Settings, tap Accessibility, tap Visibility enhancements, and then turn on Reduce animations.
